dedupe_keys.name: google cloud service health incident history with json feed

description: Google Cloud Service Health publishes the incident history of Google Cloud products, from core services such as Compute Engine, Cloud Storage and BigQuery to AI services and many deprecated products. For each incident the page gives the affected products and locations, start and end times and duration, a series of status updates and, for significant incidents, a preliminary and a full incident report with root cause and remediation. Unlike most providers, Google offers the history as machine-readable feeds: a JSON history with a published schema, a JSON product catalogue and an RSS feed, alongside the web interface. Examples from 2026 include an error-rate incident on the Vertex AI Gemini API in February lasting almost two hours and a multi-product incident in the us-west1 region in August lasting from 41 minutes to nearly three hours depending on the service. Coverage: Google Cloud regions worldwide; the depth of history is not stated on the page. Format and access: web pages, JSON and RSS, free. Caveats: only incidents Google chose to post publicly; durations are per product and overlap. Simulation uses: failure and repair time statistics for cloud services, regional outage scenarios and dependency modelling for services hosted in data centres. Related records: the AWS and Azure archives are counterparts, and the Cloud Uptime Archive collects such reports as traces.
